title: pva3DText
body:
## pva3DText

Creates polygonal (filled outline) geometry spelling Text in a vector font, lying in the x-y plane with the text starting near the origin and characters about one unit tall. It is real geometry, so it can be transformed, clipped or exported, unlike a screen-space text annotation. Use it to label parts of a 3-D scene.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- Only printable ASCII characters and "\n" line breaks are supported.
- Scale and place the text with a transform; the source has no size or position options.
- Schemaxis generates this source from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for it, so inspect the output before relying on it.

Native constructor: `a3DText`. Identity: `sources/VectorText`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

No connected inputs (source/resource).


### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Text` | This property contains the text string to be displayed. The ASCII alphanumeric characters a-z, A-Z, and 0-9 are supported; so are ASCII punctuation marks. The only supported control character is "\n", which inserts a new line in the text string. | `{"type":"string"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `"REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"` |

Execution contract:

```json
{
  "mode": "serial",
  "performance": "unknown"
}
```

Coverage and unbound native properties:

```json
{
  "defaults": "native defaults for omitted options",
  "gaps": {},
  "origin": "generated",
  "output": "native inspection required; explicit output-port selection available",
  "outputPorts": null,
  "qualification": "not-run"
}
```

### Syntax example

Place in `nodes`. Data outputs may be selected by a scene; resource outputs must be connected to a compatible consumer.

```json
{
  "id": "result",
  "filter": "pva3DText"
}
```
